errors.text_span: visually organizes a set of analytical tasks into three concentric layers, each representing a different level of analysis: the innermost “Perception Layer” (40.4%), the middle “Semantic Layer” (41.2%), and the outermost “Content Analysis” (18.4%)
errors.evidence: The chart shows four main categories in its inner ring: Perception Layer (40.4%), Semantic Layer (41.2%), Cultural Layer (14.1%), and Signal Layer (4.3%). The description incorrectly states there are three layers, misidentifies "Content Analysis" (a sub-category) as a main layer, and hallucinates the percentage "18.4%" for it.
The description completely omits two of the four main categories shown in the chart's inner ring: the "Cultural Layer (14.1%)" and the "Signal Layer (4.3%)".

errors.text_span: The outermost Content Analysis layer, also in light blue, contains tasks like Professional Knowl & Reasoning, Culture of Speaker, Imagination, Acoustic Quality Analysis, Anomaly Detection, and Audio Difference Analysis.
errors.evidence: This sentence incorrectly groups sub-tasks. The tasks from "Professional Knowl & Reasoning" to "Imagination" belong to the omitted "Cultural Layer", while "Acoustic Quality Analysis" and "Anomaly Detection" belong to the omitted "Signal Layer". They are all incorrectly placed under a fabricated "Content Analysis layer".

errors.text_span: Each task is labeled with its name and, where applicable, its percentage contribution to the respective layer.
errors.evidence: This statement is incorrect. Only the four main layers in the inner ring have percentage labels. The individual sub-category tasks in the outer rings (e.g., Music Theory, Speaker Analysis) are not labeled with percentages.
The list of sub-tasks is incomplete. It omits the task "Aesthetic Analysis", which is visible in the chart as part of the Cultural Layer.

errors.text_span: the segments are arranged in a circular, descending order by size within each layer
errors.evidence: This claim is an over-generalization. While the sub-tasks in the Semantic Layer appear ordered by size, those in the Perception Layer, for example, do not appear to be consistently sorted by size.
